sections.title: From vele to any noun
sections.content: You already know vele ("with him/her") from A2 Unit 5 — that's the -val/-vel suffix already glued onto a pronoun. -val/-vel itself means "with" in the sense of using or accompanying something, and it attaches to any noun the same way. The twist: its own "v" changes to match the sound right before it, instead of staying "v".

items.english: I eat with a knife and fork.
I eat the soup with a spoon.

sections.content: The pattern: a stem ending in a single consonant doubles that consonant instead of keeping "v" (kanál -> kanállal, not kanálvel); a vowel-final stem just adds -val or -vel, following the same back/front vowel harmony as everything else — and an a-final stem like villa or hagyma lengthens to á first, the same lengthening you already know from the accusative (alma -> almát). vele was this same suffix all along — now you can use it on any noun, not just "him/her".
